current_evidence: Not verified: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour across all agents) and the WebSearch budget were exhausted before any Arun page could be fetched, so the live list and its date could not be checked; the extracted text Grokbot captured from this PDF reads 'Planning application validation requirements wef 17/10/2024'.

issues.detail: List date 2024-10-01 is taken from PDF metadata (CreationDate), not the document text. Grokbot's own extracted text from the same PDF shows the effective date 'wef 17/10/2024'. The type-specific checklists carry different dates (Householder, Listed Building, Advertisement 01/05/24; Details Reserved by Condition 31/07/25), which the single date does not reflect.
issues.evidence: tab_items quote from docm93jijm4n20185: '1 Planning application validation requirements wef 17/10/2024'; docm93jijm4n18412: 'Details Reserved By Condition Requirements 31/07/25'.

issues.detail: Design and Access Statement is placed under 'Variation of condition s73', but the source text Grokbot quotes says the DAS does NOT apply to applications to develop land without compliance with conditions (s73). The placement inverts the rule.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt: 'This does not apply to... applications for planning permission: to develop land without compliance with conditions previously attached, made pursu[ant to s73]'.

issues.detail: Householder rows for 'Design and Access Statement', 'Schedule of works (listed building)' ('Method statement. 6.') and 'Structural Survey' ('Structural survey.') are sourced from the Listed Building Requirements List (docm93jijm4n18417), not the Householder list, so they have been attached to the wrong application type. Separately, all ~22 Full planning rows from the main list carry 'INFERRED... placed under Full planning', although the main list has a 'Types of application that require this information' column that should have been used (e.g. BNG says 'Major and non major applications'; Ecology says '10 or more dwellings'). Outline and Reserved matters therefore get almost nothing.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows source URL docm93jijm4n18417 for Householder rows; main list column header 'Types of application that require this information'.

issues.detail: Most of the 41 tab_items are submission process text, contact details or fragments rather than requirements: 'We only accept electronic plans in pdf format...', 'submitted as individual pdf's', redaction of signatures/phone numbers, 'If a document has to be redacted, it will not be possible to view it in colour', 'missing information must be provided within two weeks', the Technical Support Unit phone/email (01903 737711, planning@arun.gov.uk), Fire Statement form URL fragments ('rvice.gov.uk/government/u ploads/...'), page-header fragments ('3 Advertisement consent validation requirements 01/05/24 Information item Types of application...'), and 'Where to look for further assistance...' fragments.
issues.evidence: tab_items sections 'Submission rules' and 'Drawing / document standards'.

issues.detail: The same process rules are repeated many times across checklists: the pdf-format/scale rule appears about 7 times, the individual-pdf rule about 6 times, the redaction rule about 8 times and the two-week rule 5 times; the 1:500/1:200 block plan text appears twice. 'Photographs / Photomontages' and 'Street scene elevations' rows for Householder and Full planning share identical excerpts, as do FRA and 'Sequential / Exception Test'.

Many trigger excerpts are fragments or belong to a different item: Full planning 'Schedule of works (listed building)' uses an arboricultural method statement sentence; Full planning 'Structural Survey' is telecoms/Building Control text ('...supporting high quality communications infrastructure'); Transport ('E(g) Offices not in E( c ) between 1500 and A Transport Statement...'), Fire Statement, Foul Sewage, Open space and Drainage excerpts are garbled with URL fragments or page headers; Employment ('EMP DM1 Employment Land.'), Householder Ecology ('voids) where protected species...'), HRA ('a shadow Habitats Regulation Assessment.'), Landscaping ('is required? landscaping strategy must be submitted.') and Photographs ('when. (e.g. photographs and aerial images). 3.') have no usable trigger.

'Pre-application advice / engagement details' ('the Council's pre-application advice service.') is listed as a requirement under Householder and Full planning; it is a signpost to a service, not a validation requirement.

Pagham Harbour requirements captured only as loose tab_items and not mapped to any application type: Pagham Harbour Access Management Contribution legal agreement (net gain of residential units in Pagham Harbour buffer zones A & B), and shadow Habitats Regulations Assessment for sites in the Arun Valley Impact Risk Zone, Singleton and Cocking Tunnels buffer zone or Pagham Harbour zone A. These should appear under Full, Outline and other residential-unit applications.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'Where a development results in a net gain of residential units and is located in the Pagham Harbour buffer zones A & B, there is a requirement for a financial contribution...'.

issues.detail: Completeness could not be verified against the live source (fetch budget exhausted). Grokbot's own extracted text shows item numbers running to at least 45 in the main list (e.g. 'Protected Species and Site Survey. 22', 'Landscaping 38', '41', 'Information item 45'), while only about 22 requirements were mapped to Full planning, so local requirements (e.g. noise, contamination, lighting, air quality, affordable housing, if present) may be missing. Re-check against the PDF.
issues.evidence: Numbering visible in app_type_rows excerpts from docm93jijm4n20185.

summary: The source could not be fetched (shared web budget exhausted), so neither currency nor completeness was verified. Grokbot's own data shows clear problems: the date comes from PDF metadata (the text says wef 17/10/2024), DAS is placed under s73 although the source excludes s73, listed-building items are filed under Householder, and most tab_items are process or contact text, often duplicated.
